question: What is the primary goal of applying aseptic techniques during immunization?

options.A: To prevent pathogen contamination and subsequent infection
options.B: To speed up the vaccine administration process
options.C: To reduce the manufacturing cost of vaccines
options.D: To enhance the immunogenicity of biological products

explanation: Aseptic practices create protective barriers that keep harmful microorganisms away from vulnerable tissues during invasive procedures. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: Why is maintaining aseptic technique especially critical when administering biological products like vaccines?

options.A: Vaccines can easily support microbial growth if contaminated
options.B: Biological products automatically destroy all local bacteria
options.C: Vaccines lose their chemical color if exposed to air
options.D: Microorganisms increase the immediate efficacy of the antigen

explanation: Because vaccines provide a rich medium for pathogens, accidental introduction of bacteria can lead to severe local or systemic infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: Which term describes practices that completely eliminate all microorganisms from an area or object?
explanation: Surgical asepsis, or sterile technique, aims to remove every single microorganism to protect sterile body compartments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: Medical asepsis is best defined by which of the following clinical practices?

options.A: Destroying all endospores on environmental surfaces
options.B: Creating a completely microbe-free surgical operating suite
options.C: Sterilizing metallic surgical instruments using high pressure
options.D: Reducing the overall number and spread of pathogenic organisms

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on clean techniques that limit the transmission of pathogens from person to person or surface to person. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: What is the single most effective intervention for preventing the spread of infections in clinical settings?
explanation: Hand hygiene removes transient microorganisms acquired from patients and contaminated environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Why must an alcohol-applied injection site be allowed to dry completely before needle insertion?

options.A: To ensure the patient does not experience a cold sensation
options.B: To allow adequate contact time for effective microbial destruction
options.C: To allow the skin pores to fully close up against pressure
options.D: To prevent the vaccine liquid from changing its chemical color

explanation: Antiseptics require a specific duration of contact with the skin to effectively kill microorganisms before the barrier is breached. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: What liquid must be used to reconstitute freeze-dried vaccines like measles or BCG?

options.B: Freshly boiled and cooled borehole water

explanation: Lyophilized vaccines require their exact matching diluent to preserve chemical stability and safety. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: Which action represents a direct breach of aseptic technique during vaccine preparation?

options.A: Checking the expiry date printed on the vaccine box
options.B: Allowing the skin antiseptic to air dry before injection
options.C: Cleaning the rubber vial septum with an alcohol swab
options.D: Touching the sterile needle shaft while assembling the syringe

explanation: Touching sterile components like the needle shaft or plunger introduces skin flora into parts that will contact the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: Which practice is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among healthcare workers?

options.A: Wiping injection sites with alcohol swabs
options.D: Placing safety boxes close to the workstation

explanation: Attempting to guide a used needle back into its cap frequently results in missed entries and accidental finger punctures. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: A safety box for sharps should be managed in which of the following ways?

options.A: Stored on the floor underneath the active vaccination desk
options.B: Emptied out into regular waste bins once daily
options.C: Sealed and replaced before it crosses the maximum fill line
options.D: Compressed manually to create extra room for more needles

explanation: Overfilling safety boxes leads to protruding sharps and high risks of accidental injury during handling. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: Which color of container is universally designated for the disposal of infectious sharps?
explanation: Yellow puncture-resistant containers are standard for housing contaminated needles, lancets, and other sharp instruments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: A nurse finishes immunizing a child and holds a cotton swab stained with a small drop of blood. Into which container should this swab be placed?
explanation: Blood-stained cotton swabs are classified as infectious soft waste and belong in yellow liners, not sharp containers or municipal bins. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)
